summary: 语音变化有多种来源。语言接触和身份时尚能解释一部分变化，儿童模仿以及为省力而进行的同化、省音也会改变发音。

paragraphs.brief: 重建语音历史并寻找音变规律
sentences: All living languages undergo changes of various kinds, for which there are various reasons.
所有语言都有各种变化，原因各异。
The changes that have caused most dispute are those in pronunciation.
引起大多数争议的变化是发音变化。

We have various sources of evidence for the pronunciations of earlier times, like the evidence of spellings, the treatment of words borrowed from other languages or borrowed by them, the descriptions of contemporary grammarians, and the modern pronunciations in all the languages and dialects concerned.
我们有各种证据来证明早期的文稿，例如拼写证据、从其他语言借用或借用的文字的处理、当代语法学家的描述以及所有有关语言和方言的现代文稿。
These, combined with a knowledge of the mechanism of speech production, can often give us a very good idea of the pronunciation of an earlier age, though absolute certainty is never possible.
这些问题加上对语言制作机制的了解，往往能使我们很好地了解早期的发音，尽管绝对的确定性是不可能的。
When we study the pronunciation of a language over any period of a few generations or more, we find that it is subject to change.
当我们研究一种语言在几代人或更长时间的发音时，我们发现它可能会改变。

Moreover, there are always large-scale regularities in the changes: for example, over a period of time, all the long a sounds in a language may change into long o sounds, or all the b sounds in a certain position (for example, at the end of a word) may change into p sounds.
这些变化往往有普遍规律，例如一种语言里所有的长 a 音可能逐渐变成长 o 音，处于特定位置（如词尾）的 b 音也可能都变成 p 音。
Such regular changes are often called sound laws.
这种定期的改变往往被称为健全的法律。
There are no universal sound laws, but simply particular sound laws for one given language at one given period.
没有普遍适用的健全法律，但在一个特定时期，只对某一语言有特定的健全法律。
paragraphs.gist: 拼写、押韵等证据结合发音机制，可用来重建早期读音，跨世代比较还显示同样的音常成批变化，这种规律称为音变规律。

paragraphs.brief: 母语发音习惯怎样跨代流传
sentences: One cause of change is the influence of one language on another.
变化的原因之一是一种语言对另一种语言的影响。
We learn our mother tongue very thoroughly, and acquire a whole set of speech habits which become second nature to us.
我们非常透彻地学习我们的母语，并获得一整套语言习惯，这些习惯成为我们的第二本性。
When later we learn a foreign language, we inevitably carry over some of these speech habits into it, and so do not speak it exactly like a native.
等我们学习了外语，我们不可避免地会把一些语言习惯带到它里面，所以说起来不像本地人。
Consequently, in bilingual situations the second language tends to be modified.
因此，在双语情况下，第二种语言往往会修改。

Such modifications may not persist, of course: an isolated Polish or German immigrant to Britain will usually have grandchildren who speak English like natives because the influence of the general speech environment (playmates, school, work) is stronger than that of the home.
当然，这种修改可能不会持续下去：一个孤立的波兰或德国移民到英国时，通常会有孙子说英语像本地人一样，因为一般语言环境(同龄人、学校、工作)的影响比家庭更强。

But if a large and closely knit group of people adopt a new language, then the modifications they make in it may persist among their descendants, even if the latter no longer speak the original language that caused the changes.
但是，如果一大批紧密联系的人采用新的语言，那么他们对其语言所作的修改可能会在他们的后代中持续存在，即使后者不再说导致这些变化的原始语言。
This can be seen in Wales, where the influence of Welsh has affected the pronunciation of English, and the very characteristic melody of Welsh English has been carried over from Welsh.
威尔士就是一例，当地英语的发音受威尔士语影响，那种鲜明的语调便传承自威尔士语。
paragraphs.gist: 学新语言时人们会带入母语的发音习惯，人数众多且联系密切的群体还能把这种影响传给后代，威尔士英语的语调就是一例。

paragraphs.brief: 社会声望带动口音传播
sentences: It is also possible that fashion plays a part in the process of change.
时尚也有可能在变革过程中发挥作用。

It certainly plays a part in the spread of change: one person imitates another, and people with the most prestige are most likely to be imitated, so that a change that takes place in one social group may be imitated (more or less accurately) by speakers in another group.
时尚显然有助于变化的传播，人们会彼此模仿，尤其爱模仿有声望者，一个群体的音变便可能被其他群体的人学去，模仿的准确程度则各不相同。
When a social group goes up or down in the world, its pronunciation will gain or lose prestige.
当一个社会群体上下在世界，它的发音会增加或失去声望。

Some of the changes in accepted English pronunciation in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries have been shown to consist of the replacement of one style of pronunciation by another style already existing, and it is likely that such substitutions were a result of the great social changes of the period: the increased power and wealth of the middle classes, and their steady infiltration upwards into the ranks of the landed gentry probably carried elements of middle class dialect into upper class speech.
有研究表明，十七、十八世纪英语标准发音的一些变化，其实是一种已有读音取代另一种；当时中产阶级财富和权势增加，陆续跻身有地产的上层阶级，很可能也把自己的方言特征带进了上层社会的口语。
However, besides spreading changes that have already taken place, fashion may actually cause changes in pronunciation.
然而，除了传播已经发生的变化外，时尚实际上可能会改变发音。
In a stratified society, the important thing about a fashion is that it is exclusive: as soon as the fashion has penetrated to a lower social group, it’s time to move on.
在分层社会中，时尚的关键在于它的排他性：某种风尚一旦传入较低的社会阶层，就该换一种了。
paragraphs.gist: 口音会随群体地位的升降而获得或失去声望，模仿促使某些发音传播，十七、十八世纪英国中产阶级地位上升便可能改变了标准读音。

paragraphs.brief: 高声望群体如何保持区别
sentences: This can be seen in clothes: fashionable people may find it flattering to be imitated, but as soon as the new fashion has really caught on they must change to something else, to mark themselves off as different.
这可以从衣着中看出：时髦的人可能会觉得模仿是恭维的，但是，只要新时尚真的被抓住，他们就必须改变为别的东西，将自己标记为不同。
It may be the same with language, for social groups use characteristic styles of language to mark themselves off from other groups.
与语言一样，社会团体使用典型的语言风格，从其他团体中抹去自己的痕迹。

A group that has high prestige may find that its style of speech is being imitated by other groups, and then its members may (perhaps subconsciously) begin to change it, perhaps by exaggerating its distinguishing characteristics.
一个声望很高的团体可能会发现其他团体正在模仿其演讲风格，然后其成员(或许是潜意识的)可能开始改变它，或许是夸大了其显著特征。
paragraphs.gist: 正如引领服饰潮流者会在模仿者增多时换装，高声望群体也可能改变或夸大自身的口音特征，以维持与其他群体的区别。

paragraphs.brief: 语言接触无法解释全部音变
sentences: However, while interaction between different languages, and between the dialects of a single language, can explain some changes in pronunciation, it cannot explain them all.
然而，虽然不同语言之间和单一语言方言之间的互动可以解释读音方面的一些变化，但不能解释所有变化。
paragraphs.gist: 语言接触和方言互动能解释部分发音变化，仍有一些音变要寻找其他成因。

paragraphs.brief: 随机模仿偏差为何还不够
sentences: Another cause that has been suggested is the fact that the imitation of children is imperfect: they copy their parents’ speech, but never reproduce it exactly.
另一种解释认为，儿童对父母发音的模仿总有偏差，他们学着父母说话，却不会完全照搬。
This seems to be true enough and it moreover seems to be true that even adults show a certain amount of random variation in their pronunciation.
这似乎已经足够了，而且，甚至成年人的发音也出现了某种程度的随机变化。
However, these facts cannot explain changes in pronunciation, unless it can be shown that there is some systematic trend in the failures in imitation.
然而，这些事实不能解释读音的变化，除非能够证明在模仿失败方面存在着某种系统性趋势。
If they are merely random deviations they will cancel one another out and there will be no net change in the language.
如果只是随机偏差，他们就会相互取消，语言不会有任何净变化。
For some of these random variations to be selected at the expense of others, there must be further forces at work.
要选择其中一些随机变化而牺牲其他变化，就必须有进一步的力量在起作用。
paragraphs.gist: 儿童模仿父母并不精确，成人发音也有波动，但随机偏差会彼此抵消，只有某些偏差持续受到特定力量推动才会形成系统音变。

paragraphs.brief: 相邻音同化有助发音省力
sentences: One such force, which is often suggested, is known as the principle of ease.
人们常提到的其中一种力量被称为“省力原则”。

We are all naturally lazy, it is argued, and so we tend to take short cuts in the movements of our speech organs, to replace movements calling for great accuracy or energy by less demanding ones, to omit sounds if they are not essential for understanding, and so on.
按这种解释，人都有省力倾向，发音器官便会少动一些，用较容易的动作代替精度或力度要求高的动作，不影响理解的音有时干脆省略。
For example, the word scant was once skamt, but the m has been changed to n under the influence of the following t.
例如，scant 一词过去读作 skamt，后来受后面 t 音影响，m 音变成了 n 音。

An economy of effort has thereby been achieved, because n and t are articulated in the same place (with the tip of the tongue against the teeth-ridge), whereas m is articulated elsewhere (with the two lips).
因而实现了一种努力的经济效益，因为n和t是在同一地方表达的(舌尖对着牙脊)，而m则在别处表达(两唇)。
The change from skamt to scant would be an example of assimilation, which is a very common kind of change.
从 skamt 变为 scant，就是非常常见的音变现象“同化”的一个例子。
Assimilation is the changing of a sound under the influence of a neighbouring sound.
同化指一个音在相邻语音的影响下发生改变。
paragraphs.gist: 按发音省力原则，skamt 中的 m 受到后面 t 的影响变为 n，两者发音部位相同，连读更省力，这种邻音影响叫作同化。

paragraphs.brief: 辅音弱化与重复音节省略
sentences: Assimilation is not the only way in which we change our pronunciation in order to reduce effort.
模仿不是我们改变发音以减少努力的唯一途径。
A sound may come to be pronounced less energetically, wherever it occurs: the English r and h sounds are undoubtedly pronounced much less vigorously now than they were a thousand years ago.
一个音无论出现在哪里，都可能比以前发得更轻；例如今天的英语 r 音和 h 音就明显不如一千年前发得有力。
In some positions a sound may disappear altogether.
在某些位置上，声音可能完全消失。
At one time the t was pronounced in words like castle and Christmas, and the g in words like gnat and gnaw.
过去，人们会读出 castle、Christmas 中的 t 音，也会读出 gnat、gnaw 中的 g 音。
Sometimes a whole syllable is dropped out if it occurs twice running.
有时，同一音节连续出现两次，其中一个就会被省略。
A modern example is temporary, which in Britain is pronounced as if it were tempory.
现代的例子只是暂时的，在英国，这个例子是暂时的。
paragraphs.gist: 除了同化，发音还会减弱或消失，如 castle 的 t 不再发音，连续类似音节也可能省去一个，英国人读 temporary 即是一例。

items.en: The changes include large-scale regularities known as ________.
items.zh: 这些变化呈现出大范围的规律性，称为 ________。
items.why: 题干说“large-scale regularities known as…”,原文直接给定义: 规律性的大范围变化叫 sound laws。严格满足 =3 words,且为原文原词。

items.en: Secondly, there is the role of ________.
items.zh: 第二个因素是 ________ 所起的作用。
items.why: 空格后题干解释“某些群体有prestige,会被模仿”,这正是原文第 3段在讲: fashion 促进传播 (prestigious people are imitated)。因此填 fashion。

items.en: It has also been suggested that some changes are introduced by ________, who are unable to imitate speech in an exact way.
items.zh: 也有人认为，某些变化由 ________ 引入，因为他们无法分毫不差地模仿说话方式。
items.why: 回到对应内容“另一种解释认为，儿童对父母发音的模仿总有偏差，他们学着父母说话，却不会完全照搬”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Finally, there is a factor referred to as the ________, by which the effort necessary to produce words is reduced.
items.zh: 最后还有一个称作 ________ 的因素，它会让人们说出词语时更省力。
items.why: 原文用 the principle of ease 命名这一因素。题干已给出 the，空格中可填完整的三个词。
items.solution: 省力原则（这里指发音时倾向于少费力）

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填三个词。

items.en: It is impossible to know how words used to be pronounced.
items.zh: 我们不可能知道过去的人怎样给词语发音。
items.why: 原文说证据通常能让我们较好地推断古代发音，只是无法百分之百确定。题干把不能完全确定扩大为根本无从得知。

items.en: Some languages appear to have changed more than others.
items.zh: 有些语文的改变似乎比其他语文的改变更多。
items.why: 原文说所有活语言都会发生不同类型的变化，比较的是变化类型，没有比较各种语言的变化幅度。

items.en: Some changes in English were probably led by the middle classes.
items.zh: 英语的一些变化可能是中产阶级造成的。
items.why: 作者推测，中产阶级的经济和社会地位上升，把某些中产发音带入了上层社会，因而促成了一部分公认发音的改变。

items.en: Certain English sounds are difficult for all children to pronounce.
items.zh: 有些英语音对所有孩子来说都很难发。
items.why: 原文说儿童模仿父母说话时不会完全复制其发音。它没有指明某些英语音素，也没有说这些音对所有孩子都难发。

items.en: Scant is generally easier to pronounce than skamt.
items.zh: Scant 通常比skamt更容易发音。
items.why: n 和 t 用舌尖在同一位置发音，从 n 转到 t 比从双唇发 m 再转到 t 更省力，因此 scant 比 skamt 容易发音。

items.en: The spelling of gnat is likely to change in the future.
items.zh: gnat 这个词的拼写今后可能会改变。
items.why: 原文回顾 gnat 在过去曾经读出字母 g，讨论的是发音的历史。它没有预测这个词的拼写以后会不会改变。

items.en: The spelling of temporary no longer reflects its pronunciation.
items.zh: temporary 的拼写已不能反映它实际的读音。
items.why: 作者说英国人念 temporary 时听起来近似 tempory，字母拼写保留着读音中已省掉的一部分。

items.en: the b sound changing to a p sound at the end of words
items.zh: 词尾的 b 音变成 p 音

items.en: the melodic pronunciation of Welsh English
items.zh: 威尔士英语富有旋律的语调
items.answer: B · influence of one language on another
items.solution: 一种语言对另一种语言的影响

items.en: the disappearance of the t sound in Christmas
items.zh: Christmas 中的 t 音消失

pairs: unable to imitate speech in an exact way
无法原样模仿／从未完全准确地复现
发音更容易，体现了省力原则
题干用名词，定位句改用同词根的形容词。
第 8 段 · 第 1 句
points: 原文说所有活语言都会发生不同类型的变化，比较的是变化类型，没有比较各种语言的变化幅度。
空格后题干解释“某些群体有prestige,会被模仿”,这正是原文第 3段在讲: fashion 促进传播 (prestigious people are imitated)。因此填 fashion。
clauses: All living languages undergo changes of various kinds, ….
“for which there are various reasons”修饰前面的 changes。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 changes，再把修饰信息接回主句。
These, combined with a knowledge of the mechanism of speech production, can often give us a very good idea of the pronunciation of an earlier age, ….
连接词 though 引出“though absolute certainty is never possible”，说明主句的让步关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 though 把这一层关系补进去。
